rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Ecological pyramids and energy flow ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Ecological pyramids and energy flow** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  An **ecological pyramid** graphs a trophic property — number, biomass or energy — level by level, with producers at the base. The **10% law** (Lindeman): only about a tenth of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next; the rest is lost to respiration, waste and uneaten parts. Energy pyramids are always upright; the other two can sometimes invert.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Three pyramid types — number, biomass, energy; energy pyramid is ALWAYS upright (Lindeman 10% law); biomass inverted in the ocean (phytoplankton < fish standing crop at a moment); number inverted for a single tree's insects.  ·  Trick 2: 10% law numerical: 10,000 J producers → 1,000 J herbivore → 100 J carnivore → 10 J top — one chain calculation earns the numerical mark.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Worked example.** Producers fix 100,000 kJ/m²/yr. By the 10% law: herbivores get 10,000, first carnivores 1,000, top carnivores 100. To support one 200-kg tiger, the ecosystem must fix energy for tonnes of deer and hectares of grass.…  ·  ## 7. Exam Zone NEB past-question map (long/short), topic-wise MCQs with explanations, and short tricks (block VII). Existing entrance-exam (CEE) material stays where it is; this zone grows around it — see the seeded exam fields of this file when present.  ·  **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) State the 10% law and name Lindeman. (2) Draw the energy pyramid with numbers. (3) Which pyramids can invert, and give the ocean and tree-insect examples. (4) Why can the energy pyramid never invert? (5) Why are food chains limited to 4–5 trophic levels?

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Energy shrinks ~10× at every step; the energy pyramid is always upright, biomass and number pyramids sometimes are not. The consequence: few top predators, short chains, and plants as the energy base of everything. **Self-check:** starting from 200,000 kJ at T1, can you compute T2, T3 and T4?
